findings.explanation: The PR removes the @require_role("admin") decorator from the audit_log view (app/routes/admin.py:33), leaving only @admin_bp.route("/audit"). This endpoint is registered under url_prefix="/admin" (app/__init__.py:23), so it is an /admin endpoint. Policy §4 requires every /admin endpoint to require the admin role via @require_role("admin"). The removed decorator was the sole enforcement: require_role (app/auth.py:69-85) is the only mechanism that authenticates the bearer token and checks the role, and there is no global before_request/after_request hook or other check in the view. As a result, GET /admin/audit is now reachable by any unauthenticated caller and returns sensitive audit data (user_id, action) for all users, violating the admin-only access rule.

evidence.content:
## 4. Admin panel
- Every endpoint under `/admin` requires the **admin** role, enforced with `@require_role("admin")`.
- There are NO alternative access paths to admin functionality: no debug headers, no secret query parameters, no IP allowlists.
